summary: Reproduced a non-replannable ForwardBatch plan recorded at three rows and then padded to four while needs_forward_metadata_init remained false. Eager decode and extend now fail closed before model attention/KV writes unless the backend validates an explicit physical execution extent. DSA preserves semantic preplanning and accepts the resized batch only when its padded kernel row metadata, query/key cumulative offsets, and KV write locations cover all physical tokens. The candidate's attention-TP padding correction is retained.

tests.what_was_measured: 13 tests passed, including real EagerRunner decode and draft-extend boundaries that reject the three-to-four-row stale plan before model.forward, plus DSA acceptance/rejection based on concrete four-row kernel and KV extents. Raw output: reports/j-04c9f1d479a7/raw/focused-tests-final.txt

On AMD Instinct MI350X, GPU-resident DSA metadata for three real rows and attention TP 2 was [11, 12, 13, 0], equal to an independent ceiling-alignment reference with four physical rows. Raw output: reports/j-04c9f1d479a7/raw/gpu-reference.txt
Repository formatting, lint, test registration taxonomy, and source checks. Raw output: reports/j-04c9f1d479a7/raw/pre-commit-final.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X, ROCm 7.2.26015; the focused GPU test and independent GPU tensor reference both executed successfully.

remaining_limitations: No model-weight end-to-end speculative DSA run was performed, so full speculative model correctness is not claimed. Validation covers the actual ForwardBatch/EagerRunner/backend boundary and concrete DSA/KV row extents. CUDA-only architectures were not exercised. No FlyDSL C++ or other native source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
